description: Verify that DUT's ICMP Echo Reply data field exactly equals the data field that the Echo Request carried — payload must be echoed verbatim (RFC 792 Echo Request/Reply MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
Echo Reply has no semantic transformation of the payload — the exact bytes the requester sent must come back. This is what makes ping useful for liveness, latency and MTU probing: the sender knows what it sent and can verify what came back.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ICMP Echo Request with a known payload (e.g. an ASCII pattern or sequence)

2. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: ICMP Echo Reply
      - data field == request payload, byte-for-byte   ← key check

[Pass condition]
Reply payload equals the Request payload exactly.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_payload_mismatch — Reply was emitted but its data field differs from what was sent
• Fail_timeout — DUT did not emit a Reply within the window

verdicts.Pass: Reply payload matched request — normal echo
verdicts.Fail_payload_mismatch: Reply payload differed from request — echo not byte-for-byte
verdicts.Fail_timeout: DUT did not emit a Reply within the window
